name: The Bowes Museum
known: Founded by John Bowes and his wife Joséphine Benoîte Coffin-Chevallier, Countess of Montalbo.
The Wolfson Foundation funds the redevelopment of three founder galleries;

name: Holburne Museum
known: Individual giving is organised in a Director's Circle, Major Donors, Patrons and an 1882 Circle (holburne.org supporters page).
Posts trustees' reports and signed accounts for 2016 to 2024, names its eleven directors and keeps a named supporters list with no date.

name: Belfast Exposed
known: Programmes: a photography training programme, a therapeutic photography programme for mental health and wellbeing, youth programmes, and Futures, a mentoring and exhibiting programme for early-career artists and curators (Belfast Exposed).

name: Golden Thread Gallery
known: Run by Co-Directors Peter Richards, director since 2002, and Sarah McAvera, co-director since 2024 (Wikipedia).

name: Eastside Projects
known: Current directors are Ruth Claxton and Gavin Wade (Wikipedia).

name: Ikon Gallery
known: Founded by the collector Angus Skene with four Birmingham School of Art artists, David Prentice, Sylvani Merilion, Jesse Bruton and Robert Groves.
Jonathan Watkins directed the gallery from 1999 to 2022, and Ian Hyde is chief executive (Wikipedia).

name: Arnolfini
known: In 2017 it lost its £750,000 annual Arts Council England grant after an assessment that it was "not viable"; the funding was reinstated in 2019 under executive director Gary Topp (Wikipedia).

name: Kettle's Yard
known: Founded by Jim Ede and his wife Helen, who moved to Cambridge in 1956 and, with help from Winton Aldridge, converted four small cottages into one house for Ede's collection.

name: Chapter
known: Founded by the Welsh artists Christine Kinsey and Bryan Jones with the journalist Mike Flood.

Sharon Stone, Chapter's director of finance, told the Senedd culture committee in October 2024: "We've gone from close to £680,000 a year to £390,000 a year", and pointed to a 43% cut in the latest funding round (Caerphilly Observer).

name: Grizedale Arts
known: Adam Sutherland became director in 1999 and merged the Society into the new Grizedale Arts that year (Wikipedia).
